nodes.content: For t=1,...,T: output x_t in V subset R^d; pay loss ell_t(x_t), ell_t:V->R; then receive feedback on ell_t.
nodes.relevance: Loss is not known before output. The chosen witness is deterministic and fixed in advance.

nodes.content: Regret_T(u) := sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t) - sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(u), for u in V.
Losses are adversarial; future knowledge is not assumed. Restrictions may be placed on the loss class.
V subset R^d is convex iff for every x,y in V and lambda in (0,1), lambda*x+(1-lambda)*y belongs to V.
For an extended-real-valued function f on R^d, dom f = {x in R^d : f(x)<+infinity}.
f:R^d->[ -infinity,+infinity ] is convex iff its epigraph {(x,y) in R^(d+1): y>=f(x)} is convex.
Affine functions f(x)=<z,x>+b are convex.
nodes.provenance: Available standing semantic support, not explicitly cited in Theorem 5.4 proof.

nodes.content: A function is proper if it is nowhere -infinity and finite somewhere.
For proper f:R^d->(-infinity,+infinity], g in R^d is a subgradient of f at x iff f(y)>=f(x)+<g,y-x> for all y in R^d.
The set of subgradients at x is denoted partial f(x); f is subdifferentiable at x iff this set is nonempty.
f is L-Lipschitz on V subset dom f with respect to norm ||.|| iff |f(x)-f(y)| <= L||x-y|| for all x,y in V.

Require nonempty closed convex V subset R^d, x_1 in V, eta_1,...,eta_T>0. For t=1,...,T output x_t, pay subdifferentiable loss ell_t(x_t), select g_t in partial ell_t(x_t), update x_{t+1}=Pi_V(x_t-eta_t*g_t)=argmin_{y in V}||x_t-eta_t*g_t-y||_2.
nodes.specialization: Unprojected means V=R^d and update x_{t+1}=x_t-eta_t*g_t. Source uses Euclidean geometry.

nodes.content: If we want to use time-varying learning rates, we need to control the terms ||x_t-u||_2^2. To do it, we assume a bounded domain V. However, this assumption is false in most of the machine learning applications. We will also see in Section 5.2 that this is not an artifact of the proof, that is, OGD can fail in unbounded domains with time-varying learning rates. That said, in the stochastic setting, you can still use a time-varying learning rate in SGD with an unbounded domain, as we will see in Chapter 3.
nodes.exactness: Words transcribed verbatim; mathematical typography normalized. The source says OGD here, OSD in Theorem 5.4.
nodes.scope: Existential failure, not failure of every time-varying schedule or of stochastic SGD.

nodes.content: Focus on OSD and show that the Chapter 2 bounded-domain limitation for time-varying stepsizes is real. Theorem 5.4 supplies a lower bound.
phi(alpha) := 1/(2-alpha) + ((1/2)^(1-alpha)-1)/(1-alpha), for alpha in (0,1).
For every alpha in (0,1), 0 < phi(alpha) < 1-ln 2.

nodes.content: For alpha in (0,1), and integer horizon T >= 2/((1-alpha)*phi(alpha)), unprojected OSD with eta_t=t^(-alpha), x_1=0 admits a sequence of T convex and 1-Lipschitz losses for which Regret_T(0) >= (1/2)*phi(alpha)*T^(2-alpha).
Assume d=1. For d>=2 embed the one-dimensional loss vectors in the first coordinate of R^d.

nodes.content: Let m=ceil(T/2), n=floor(T/2). Set ell_t(x)=-x for 1<=t<=m and ell_t(x)=x for m+1<=t<=T. There are m negative-slope losses followed by n positive-slope losses.

nodes.content: The displayed affine losses are convex, 1-Lipschitz, and subdifferentiable. Their subgradients are -1 and +1, respectively. In R^d these are -e_1 and +e_1 and Lipschitz is with respect to the Euclidean norm.

nodes.content: For 1<=t<=m, x_{t+1}=x_t+t^(-alpha).
x_t=sum_{i=1}^{t-1} i^(-alpha), for 1<=t<=m+1, from x_1=0.
For m+1<=t<=T, x_{t+1}=x_t-t^(-alpha).
x_t=x_{m+1}-sum_{i=m+1}^{t-1}i^(-alpha)=sum_{i=1}^m i^(-alpha)-sum_{i=m+1}^{t-1}i^(-alpha), for m+1<=t<=T+1.
Regret_T(0)=-sum_{t=1}^m x_t+sum_{t=m+1}^T x_t. All ell_t(0)=0.
Regret_T(0)=-sum_{t=1}^m sum_{i=1}^{t-1}i^(-alpha)+sum_{t=m+1}^T (sum_{i=1}^m i^(-alpha)-sum_{i=m+1}^{t-1}i^(-alpha)).
Regret_T(0)=-sum_{i=1}^m (m-i)/i^alpha+n*sum_{i=1}^m i^(-alpha)-sum_{i=m+1}^T (T-i)/i^alpha.
Regret_T(0)=-sum_{i=1}^m (m-n)/i^alpha+sum_{i=1}^T i^(1-alpha)-T*sum_{i=m+1}^T i^(-alpha).
ceil(T/2)-floor(T/2)<=1.

nodes.content: Regret_T(0)>=-1-integral_1^m x^(-alpha) dx + integral_0^T x^(1-alpha) dx - T*integral_m^T x^(-alpha) dx.
nodes.source_typography: The first integral lower annotation is printed i=1 although integration variable is x. Semantic lower endpoint 1 is recorded without silently altering the facsimile.
nodes.logic: AND: all three integral comparisons and the parity bound are jointly used.

Regret_T(0)>=-1+1/(1-alpha)-m^(1-alpha)/(1-alpha)+T^(2-alpha)/(2-alpha)-(T^(2-alpha)-T*(T/2)^(1-alpha))/(1-alpha).

logic_notes: There is one source proof route for the regret bound.
The three integral comparisons are AND inputs, not alternative routes.

Dimension cases d=1 and d>=2 are exhaustive cases. A fixed dimension chooses one branch, but proving the universally quantified statement requires both cases; the high-dimensional branch depends on the scalar proof.
The range assertion is needed for threshold positivity; its omitted proof is exposed as G-PHI-RANGE.
Limit and numerical supplement are sibling conclusions, not premises of the regret bound. The 0.3 comparison is not a uniform lower bound on phi(alpha).
